previous_statement: Convergence, exactness, and the unit. Choose a_corr>0 so K_N*a_corr<=1/4 and the final distance below is <1-a_corr. Starting with S_0=T, apply node 1.2.2 recursively. With b_0<=a and b_{k+1}<=K_N b_k^2, one has b_k<=a*2^{-k} after decreasing a_corr if necessary. The telescoping estimate ||S_{k+1}-S_k||_cb<=2b_k makes S_k converge in cb norm to one dagger-preserving linear map mu with ||mu-T||_cb<=4a. Passing to the limit in the defect identity gives mu(xy)=mu(x)mu(y), and amplification commutes with the limit, so ||mu_n-T_n||<=4a for all n. Also ||mu(I)-I||<=||mu(I)-T(I)||+||T(I)-I||<=5a<1. Since mu(I) is a self-adjoint idempotent in B(H), either mu(I)=I or I-mu(I) is a nonzero projection of norm one; the strict bound forces mu(I)=I. Thus node 1.2 holds with C_corr=4 and this universal a_corr.
new_statement: Convergence, exactness, and the unit. Choose a_corr>0 so K_N*a_corr<=1/4, 6*a_corr<1, and 7*a_corr<1. Starting with S_0=T, apply node 1.2.2 recursively. With b_0<=a and b_{k+1}<=K_N*b_k^2, one has b_k<=a*2^{-k}; the telescoping estimate ||S_{k+1}-S_k||_cb<=3b_k gives ||S_k-S_0||_cb<=6a<1, so node 1.2.1 and ||S_0||_cb<=2 imply ||S_k||_cb<=3 and justify every iteration. Thus S_k converges in cb norm to one dagger-preserving linear map mu with ||mu-T||_cb<=6a. Passing to the limit gives mu(xy)=mu(x)mu(y), and amplification commutes with the limit, so ||mu_n-T_n||<=6a for all n. Also ||mu(I)-I||<=7a<1. Since mu(I) is a self-adjoint idempotent in B(H), either mu(I)=I or I-mu(I) is a nonzero projection of norm one; the strict bound forces mu(I)=I. Thus node 1.2 holds with C_corr=6 and this universal a_corr.
